title: The colour code boxes on Branding show no focus ring when reached with the keyboard
what: The boxes where the owner types the brand colour code and the background tone code turn off the browser's focus outline, and their frame does not change when they have the focus. A keyboard user cannot see which box is selected until they start typing.
expected: Every box shows a clear ring or frame change when it gets the keyboard focus, in the dark and the light look.
how_often: every time a keyboard is used
fix_line: Show the accent ring on the colour code boxes when they have the focus.

title: The admin app ignores the bigger text setting in the computer browser
what: Every text size in the admin app is a fixed number of screen dots, set on each piece of text. If an owner sets the browser's text size to large, the admin app stays the same size. Page zoom still works. The smallest notes on Branding are 11 and 12 dots.
expected: Text grows when the browser's text size setting is raised, and stays readable at the largest setting.
how_often: every time, for anyone using bigger browser text
fix_line: Size text from the browser's base size instead of fixed dots.

title: In the light look, the 'No logo yet' words are hard to read
what: The logo box is always painted in the member app's dark background, but the 'No logo yet' words inside it use the admin app's grey for quiet words. In the light look that grey is dark, so it sits at about 3.4 to 1 on the near-black box. Small words need at least 4.5 to 1.
expected: The words inside the logo box read at 4.5 to 1 or better in both the dark and the light look.
how_often: every time in light mode before a logo is added
fix_line: Use a light word colour inside the dark logo box.

title: Which of the other logo colours is picked is shown only by a slightly different frame
what: Under the suggested colour, the other colours from the logo are plain coloured squares. The one in use gets a frame of a different shade, the same thickness, with no tick. A screen reader hears only a colour code, such as 'Use this colour: #3A7BD5', not a colour name.
expected: The picked square is clearly marked by more than colour (a tick or a thicker frame), and each square says something a person can picture.
how_often: every time a logo has more than one colour
fix_line: Add a tick to the picked square and a plain colour name to each.

title: The two logo choices behave like a pick-one list for a screen reader, but the arrow keys do nothing
what: After the background is taken off a logo, the 'Without the background' and 'Keep my logo as it is' cards tell a screen reader they are a pick-one list. In such a list people expect the arrow keys to move between choices. Here the arrow keys do nothing, and each card is a separate Tab stop.
expected: Either the arrow keys move between the two choices, or the cards are announced as plain buttons.
who: owners using a keyboard or screen reader
how_often: every time a plain logo background is taken off
fix_line: Add arrow key movement to the two logo choices.
